subject: Post-call: Multilingual model fit & evals — EU/APAC follow-up
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@globexretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ravi Menon <ravi.menon@globexretail.com>
Date: 2027-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up + ask: multilingual evals for EU/APAC locales

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — really helpful to see Redwood's routing and caching in action. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can scope the POC: 

- Primary use case: localized product descriptions and customer support summarization across DE/FR/ES (EU) and JA/KO/EN-AU (APAC).
- Key SLOs: 95th pctile latency < 350ms for short responses, and token cost target to hit within your recommended Dedicated configs.
- Concern: we saw quality drops for German idioms in a quick test — want to validate model fit across these locales.

Requests:
1) Can you share your recommended model(s) and quantization for this mix of languages?
2) Any existing benchmark links for EU/APAC languages?
3) A prompt set we can run on our side for regression checks (we can return results).

Attached a short sample of 40 US/DE/FR/JA test prompts we ran yesterday (see attached). We can also share more examples after you confirm which model to evaluate.

Thanks,
Sara
Sr. Product Manager, International Growth
Globex Retail

Attachment: globex-sample-40.txt (text)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@globexretail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-15T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up + ask: multilingual evals for EU/APAC locales

Hi Sara — great to meet you this morning; appreciate the clear priorities.

Quick answers up front:
- Recommended models: start with rdx-llama-3-13b-multilingual (FP16) for balance of cost/quality. For tight latency you can try rdx-llama-3-7b-quant (int8) but expect some edge-case degradation on low-resource scripts (KO/JA).
- Quantization: int8 config "q4_0" is a good first pass; our recommendation PDF (attached) maps model/quant options to expected token cost and latency.
- Benchmarks & prompt set: uploading a curated prompt set and our latest language-specific benchmark report to Drive — links below.

Next steps I propose:
1) We run an internal eval using your sample prompts + our prompt-set-eu-apac.md (attached) across three variants (13b FP16, 13b int8, 7b int8).
2) We'll share a CSV with per-locale quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE + human spot checks) and latency/cost numbers.
3) Schedule follow-up deep-dive next Tue for results + POC sizing.

I've looped Neha (in infra/model optimization) to flag any locale-specific regression risk and Vanessa for commercial/POC scoping.

Links:
- Benchmark report: https://docs.redwood.ai/benchmarks/multilingual/2027-07-report
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-eval-results

Attachments: prompt-set-eu-apac.md (markdown), recommended-models-and-quantization.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sara Liu <sara.liu@globexretail.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-15T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up + ask: multilingual evals for EU/APAC locales

Thanks — jumping in with technical notes from the eval team.

High-level: the 13b multilingual checkpoint performs well across DE/FR/ES for generation tasks we measured, but we have two important caveats: \n
- German idiomatic expressions: our automated metrics underweight idiom preservation; human evals show a ~6-8% drop in adequacy for idioms versus en-US. We'll include targeted idiom prompts in the prompt set.
- Japanese/Korean: tokenization differences and pretraining corpora coverage can cause hallucination in very terse prompts. For these locales we recommend adding 1-2-shot examples in the prompt set (we included examples in prompt-set-eu-apac.md).

Operational notes:
- If you need strict latency at 95th < 350ms, we should provision Dedicated instances with accelerated NVLink pairing; we'll provide a sample autoscale policy tuned for bursty traffic.
- Caching: prefix caching will help for repeated catalog snippets; consider a short TTL (10-30s) for dynamic product lines.

I'll run the tri-model eval this afternoon and push results as multilingual-eval-results-v1.csv to the Drive link Marissa posted. Please tell us if you want additional human evaluation on a subset (we can coordinate 50-100 samples).

-Neha
Senior Applied ML Engineer, Inference Optimization
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up + ask: multilingual evals for EU/APAC locales

Sara — thanks for the clear asks. On the commercial side:

- I'll draft a POC SOW that includes 2 weeks of evaluation, shared infra (hosted + optional Dedicated sizing), and up to 1000 eval tokens on our side for human spot checks.
- Pricing note: for the initial POC we can provide a pilot discount on Dedicated pricing; details in the SOW.

Best,
